PyTorch supports a jointly trained item representation combining an ID embedding with a learned text encoder; sharing that representation between GRU4Rec inputs and candidate scoring keeps one network. Implementation inference: encode only unique item IDs across histories and sampled targets, then reconstruct positions using `torch.unique(..., return_inverse=True)`. This reduces repeated text computation, although `unique` sorts internally even with `sorted=False`, so savings depend on repetition. Preserve gradients through reconstruction. [torch.unique documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.unique.html)

For text pooling, use masked sum divided by a nonpadding count clamped to at least one; explicitly zero empty-text outputs after any biased projection. `EmbeddingBag` offers pooled embeddings without materializing the complete token-embedding tensor. Standard `Embedding.weight` is a learnable item-by-dimension matrix: a custom composite module must deliberately preserve the diagnostic interface, and exposing only its ID table would omit text features. Avoid rebuilding a full differentiable catalog matrix whenever `.weight` is accessed. [EmbeddingBag documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.modules.sparse.EmbeddingBag.html), [Embedding documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Embedding)

Engineering recommendation: during evaluation, build detached composite catalog embeddings in bounded chunks, then score candidate IDs or catalog chunks from the same representation. Cache only while parameters and evaluation behavior remain fixed; invalidate after optimizer updates, checkpoint loads, device/dtype changes, or returning to training. Never reuse detached cached representations for training. Catalog storage costs approximately `items × dimensions × bytes_per_element`; chunking limits temporary encoding memory, while streaming scores avoids allocating the complete user-by-catalog matrix. These are implementation recommendations, not measured speedups or evidence of validation gains.
